title: Drive trip that cannot be reset
summary: A latched drive trip is cleared in two steps: remove the cause, then acknowledge.

sections.heading: Why reset does nothing
sections.body: While the cause (for example a jam or overload) is present, most drives refuse to acknowledge the fault. Resetting again and again does not help and can stress the machine.

sections.heading: Order of work
sections.body: Read the fault, remove the cause, acknowledge, then verify the function. Note the fault for the commissioning report.

modeled: Generic VFD behavioral model: local/remote control place, ready chain (supply, no fault, run enable), run command, latched trip with acknowledge, terminal or keypad speed reference with a preset speed, ready/running/remote/fault relays
approximated: Linear acceleration ramp, immediate deceleration, simple motor current
omitted: Fieldbus control and its communication monitoring
Safe torque off and other safety functions

repair: Remove the cause, then acknowledge the fault
troubleshooting.explanation: Acknowledging a fault is not a repair; it only confirms that the cause has been removed.
